content:
Hey guys, just saying hi and introducing myself. Stockholm University undergrad student learning lean in the Stockholm Lean User Group (SLUG). mostly focused on the c.s. courses but wanted to try lean out as well.

One question about the natural number game for multiplication. I wanted to prove associativity. However, I ended up with something like this

a + b + c +d = a + d+ c + b

And this was the example but it was much more variables. and I went about it in a very strange way.

rw [add_assoc (a+b ) (c) d]
a + b + (c +d )
rw [add_comm c d]
a + b + (d +c )
rw [← add_assoc]
a + b + d +c

Which as you can see the d is in 3rd position so I would have to do the loop again. in my actual proof I had to do that 12 times. Which made me think i was doing it an awful way. Haha. Any tips?

Well outside of the game such a goal can be solved with a single tactic (ring/lia/grind/...) so I wouldn't worry about perfecting this manual rw method.
As for the game, can you specify which level you're at and what you did to get to this goal?
If you're on the last level of multiplication world, FWIW the game's official proof for this level uses a total of 7 rewrites, so if you solved it with 12 that's pretty good!

ah I see I see. so I was supposed to do the heavy lifting so i can appreciate the better tools when I get them. Thanks for the tip. Curious where the official proofs aka answer sheets are? would like to compare mine.
It's in the game's repo, e.g. this is the solution for multiplication associativity
haha neat. fun level. thought i was going crazy. thanks!
But it looks like they were doing additive associativity, which is much easier if you induct on the right variable...
